note_sections.t: Persistent elevation of prostate-specific antigen warrants reassessment following a previously positive biopsy.

At 67 years of age, this retired postal worker entered the clinical pipeline after an incidental PSA rise surfaced in 2022. Married and cohabiting with his partner, he maintains a rigorous fitness regimen that includes three weekly five-kilometre runs. His lower urinary tract symptoms remain stable, characterized mainly by moderate frequency and nocturia. A 35 pack-year smoking history ended in 2006. Hypertension is currently controlled using valsartan, lisinopril, and metoprolol. A recent endocrinology visit for standard thyroid screening returned normal results. He explicitly denies unexplained weight fluctuations, skeletal discomfort, or blood in the urine.

DRE: Normal examination; symmetrically enlarged gland with uniform smoothness, lacking palpable asymmetry or discrete nodules. Vital signs show stable hemodynamics at 142/86 mmHg and a regular pulse of 69 bpm. Systemic review reveals no lymphadenopathy or abdominal masses.
